I'm 37, been farming this land in Quzhou County for 15 years now. My family — five of us — depends on these 10.1 mu. I've got middle school education, so I know a bit from the extension pamphlets they hand out, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors do more than what some book says.

**How I think about this year:**

It's the start of the season, so I'm looking at winter wheat first. The wheat goes in around early October. Last year my wheat yielded about 420 kg per mu, which was decent but not great — we had that dry spell in spring. The soil on my plot is okay, not the best in the village but not the worst either. Old Wang down the road, his wheat always does well, he puts about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, split into base and topdress. The extension guy told us 15 kg N per mu is enough, but I've tried that and it looks a bit yellow at jointing. So I do closer to 18-19 kg total. I buy compound fertilizer for the base — about 50 kg per mu of the 15-15-15 stuff, that's roughly 7.5 kg N, plus some P and K. Then at jointing I topdress with urea, about 20-22 kg per mu, which gives another 10 kg or so of N. Total around 18 kg N per mu. I know it's a bit more than recommended, but I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad yield. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps.

For irrigation, I've got the well, but pumping costs money. Electricity isn't cheap. I usually irrigate wheat three times: once before winter to help establishment, once at green-up in spring, and once at jointing or booting. If it's a wet spring, maybe I skip one, but I can't count on rain anymore. Last spring was too dry, so I'll plan for three times again.

My household labor is me, my wife, and my parents help out. My kid is in school. We do most work ourselves. For wheat, family labor is about 12 days total across the season — planting, fertilizing, irrigating, spraying, harvesting. I might hire a combine for harvest, that's the custom here. Planting is mid-October, harvest early June.

Now the summer maize — this is where timing gets tight. Once that wheat comes off in early June, I've got maybe 5-7 days to get the maize in the ground. No time for fancy tillage. I usually do minimal tillage — maybe a light pass with the rotary tiller, or sometimes I just plant directly if the wheat stubble isn't too thick. Neighbor Zhang did no-till last year and his maize was fine, saved him time and diesel. I'm thinking I'll try that, or at least very minimal tillage. Time is money here.

For maize fertilizer, I use compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15, so around 6 kg N. Then at the big喇叭口期 (big trumpet stage), I topdress with urea, about 15-20 kg per mu, so another 7-9 kg N. Total around 15-16 kg N per mu. I could push it to 18 like the big farms do, but maize is a bit more forgiving than wheat, and honestly after buying wheat inputs my cash is tighter by June. The maize seed — I buy hybrid seed from the local dealer, about 3 kg per mu, costs around 45 yuan per mu. I don't save seed, hybrids don't work that way.

Maize irrigation — if the summer rains are good, maybe I only irrigate once or twice. Last year I irrigated twice, once at the V6 stage and once at tasseling. But the weather has been unpredictable. I'll plan for two times, maybe three if it's really dry in July. I can't afford to let it drought-stress at tasseling, that's when you lose yield.

Pesticide — for wheat, I spray herbicide once in spring for weeds, and sometimes a fungicide if I see disease. For maize, I usually do a pre-emergence herbicide and maybe an insecticide if the borers show up. I budget about 30 yuan per mu for pesticides on each crop.

Tillage for wheat — I plow after the maize harvest in October. For maize, as I said, minimal tillage after wheat harvest because of the tight window.

Labor for maize is less intensive day-to-day but the planting window is stressful. Maybe 8 family days plus I hire a planter operator or use my own small planter. Harvest is by machine, hired.

Total input costs — I'm watching this carefully. Wheat seed plus fertilizer plus irrigation pumping plus pesticide plus machine hire is about 380-400 yuan per mu. Maize is about 320-350 yuan per mu. Total for 10.1 mu, roughly split 5 mu wheat and 5.1 mu maize, so total input cost around 3,600-3,800 yuan for the year. That's a big chunk of our cash. I can't spend more than that and still have money for my kid's school and emergencies.

Yield expectations — if the weather cooperates, I hope for 450 kg/mu on wheat and 500 kg/mu on maize. That's optimistic but achievable. If I get 400 and 450 respectively, I'll still be okay. Last year was 420 and 480, so I'm hoping for similar or slightly better.
